confirmed: Read the entire local markdown, including Appendix A, and checked the relevant PDF pages; the PDF is arXiv:2311.10127v1 dated 16 Nov 2023, with 14 pages, matching the recorded title and authors (p. 1; Appendix A, pp. 12-14).

Study 1 is an online within-person experiment with non-generative hints: EXP3 chooses among three vocabulary-based algorithms producing five-word hints; other is an appropriate design class for this out-of-scope human intervention (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1-3.2; p. 5, section 3.3).

The human concept-condition pairing and task order were counterbalanced; random assignment is not stated, so assignment.randomized = not_stated and n_randomized = null are supported (p. 5, section 3.3 Procedure).

37 University of Wisconsin-Madison undergraduates completed Study 1 and 36 were analyzed after one exclusion; the same 36 completed both conditions and are below the 50-person threshold (p. 4, section 3.3; p. 5, sections 3.3-3.4).
S1-O1 reported values match: hinted median 34, unhinted median 26.5, beta = 8.0, p < 0.001; Table 1 gives chi-square = 12.1, df = 1, Pr = 0.00047 for m versus m0 (p. 5, section 3.4 and Table 1).

S1-O2 reported values and preprocessing match: median word-type counts 57 hinted and 42 unhinted, p < 0.01, following case-folding, stopword removal, stemming, and lemmatization; these are within-participant counts, not across-person diversity (p. 6, section 3.4).

Study 2 uses GPT-4 as the respondent, with 60 model runs and 15 per condition-by-concept cell; its recorded hinted-versus-unhinted contrast is model_only. Experiments used the OpenAI API in early May 2023 with default temperature 1; no exact snapshot is stated (pp. 7-8, sections 4-4.1).

S2-O1 reported values match: hinted median 31 and unhinted median 25; the text gives p < 0.001 and Table 3 gives F = 13.816 and Pr(>F) = 0.0004558 for m versus m0 (p. 8, section 4.2; p. 9, Table 3 and following paragraph).

The one-line finding accurately reports the 36-person analysis, medians 34 and 26.5, beta = 8.0, p < 0.001, non-generative assistance, and absence of a stated random assignment procedure (pp. 3-5, sections 3.1-3.4).

The stated duration discrepancy is real: the procedure says two 20 minute sessions, whereas the instruction screenshot says 0.33 minutes per concept (p. 5, section 3.3; p. 12, Figure 5, inspected in the PDF).
Appendix A contains interface/instruction screenshots and hint-algorithm pseudocode, with no additional outcome statistics or standard errors (pp. 12-14).
This is an original two-study paper, not a synthesis; leaving synthesis counts and pooled-estimate fields empty is appropriate (pp. 3-9, sections 3-4).
summary: No randomized human generative-AI assistance study was found: 36 humans were analyzed, and 60 GPT-4 runs were simulations. The reported statistics match the PDF, but eligibility/context coding, the exclusion field, the simulation-unit count, and Intuit support require corrections.
